_README: EXPECTED-RED LEDGER. Every gate that is RED must appear here with a
MEASURED watermark, an owner and a review_by date. This is what lets CI
ask 'is anything red that we did not already record, or REDDER than we
recorded?' instead of 'is anything red?', which was a constant and
This ledger SOFTENS NOTHING. The gates still print RED, first, on every
run. What it changes is the exit code, so a NEW break is distinguishable
- a RED gate not listed here      -> FAIL (it is new)
- a RED gate worse than watermark -> FAIL (it regressed)
- a GREEN gate still listed here  -> FAIL (stale; delete the entry)
- past review_by                  -> FAIL (re-measure or sign an extension)
review_by is the anti-wallpaper clause: an expected-red gate must not

Gate 6R.bar: every implemented standard named with the DATED edition the reviewer held, e.g. 'ISO 12217-1:2022'
Gate 6R.measured_on: navalai/rules/review.py, both entries read 'edition not recorded — set this'
Gate 6R.verify: python -m pytest tests/test_phase6r.py -q  (and: python -c "from navalai.rules.review import edition_defects; print(edition_defects())")
why_red: GAP D8. This gate WAS GREEN, and it should not have been. review.py's
own docstring states 'a confirmation that cannot say WHO checked WHICH
edition is not a review, it is a rumour' — and then is_complete()
checked `reviewer` and `confirmed` and NOT `editions`, whose two values
both read 'edition not recorded — set this'. The parity gate was green
on a record that admits in its own field values that it cannot name the
document it checked.
is_complete() now requires every edition to be set and to carry a year.
That FLIPPED THIS GATE RED on 2026-08-06. Under honesty rule 6 that is
the correct outcome and not a regression: the check got stricter, the
underlying state did not get worse. Nothing was softened to absorb it —
the row prints RED, first, on every run.
CLEARING CONDITION, and it costs no compute: a reviewer writes the two
dated editions into REVIEW['editions'], deletes this entry, and flips
the row in navalai/gates.py. tests/test_phase6r.py already asserts that
a properly filled record completes, so the clearing condition is
executable rather than prose.
AND NOTE WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT ANSWER (gap D9). Its scope is
THRESHOLD parity: does our number equal the standard's number.
BuildPlan Gate 6's bar is VERDICT parity — the same verdict as a
qualified reviewer on at least three reference designs, hand
calculated. Zero reference designs and zero hand calculations exist,
and the reviewer of record is the project owner reviewing his own code
with no qualification recorded. Clearing 6R does not open Gate 6.
Gate 6R-mech is a SEPARATE, GREEN row: the mechanics around the record
(basis routing, no unreviewed basis leaking 'standard', our own
practice values not blessed by a green gate) are genuinely verified.

why_red: SUPERSEDES 75.0 FROM N=8, AND THE NEW NUMBER IS WORSE BECAUSE THE OLD
ONE WAS AN ANECDOTE. Eight hulls is not a sample. At N=18 only 5 are
clean by the checkMesh bars: 5/18 = 27.8%. Do not read the drop from
75.0 as a regression; nothing got worse, the measurement got honest.
FAILURE TAXONOMY at N=18, which is worth more than the percentage:
checkmesh-wrong-oriented  7    checkmesh-zero-volume  3
checkmesh-skewness        1    mesh-build-failed      1
solver-stopped-short      1    ok                     5
Eleven of twelve rejections are checkMesh QUALITY, not snappy failing
to produce a mesh. The mesher works; it was being asked for a mesh it
could not build.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED (commit 48e190b): _MAX_LAYERS was 10 and
n_layers_to_bridge derived 8-10 for every hull while snappy achieved
3.9-8.1 -- not one hull hit its request, and a PARTIAL stack is the
documented cell-folding mechanism. Same hull, same seed, only the
layer request changed: hull 0 at n=10 gave 12 zero-volume and 92
wrongly-oriented faces; at n=7, zero and zero. Hull 12 went 258
wrongly-oriented to 0. Over the 16 hulls common to both runs, 14/16
are clean against 5/18.
THIS WATERMARK IS THEREFORE PRE-FIX AND RE-MEASUREMENT IS OWED. It is
recorded at the configuration that produced it (LESSONS defect class
6) rather than at the one now shipped. The 14/16 was measured with the
backoff LADDER (requests 3-10 per hull), which is not the shipped
single-shot cap of 7 -- quoting it as the watermark would be a number
from a configuration the product does not run.
AND THE 'CONVERGES' HALF IS STILL UNMEASURED, as it was in 2026-08-05.
Every figure here is MESH quality. The bar is 'meshes AND converges';
19 solves were attempted and coarse cases ran 30-47 min against a ~15
min expectation in CLAUDE.md, so a full solve batch is a machine-day.
HOW THE CAP CAME TO BE WRONG, recorded because it will recur: the KCS
layer measurement (n=3 clean / n=5 solves / n=7 dies) WAS recorded and
WAS correctly marked SUPERSEDED -- it was taken on the old 38:1
anisotropic background the mesh rebuild retired. Raising the cap 3->10
was right to discard it. What never happened is the REPLACEMENT
measurement on the new family. A superseded number is not a licence to
guess the new one.
CORRECTED 2026-08-11 by an adversarial validation of the cap-7 arm:
- the verify recipe here OMITTED --solve, so counting why=='ok' returned
0 and this entry could not reproduce its own watermark;
- measured_on said np=1, the artifact records np=10;
- 27.8% is a SOLVE rate over 18 hulls and must never be compared with a
MESH rate. The like-for-like pair is 35.0% -> 70.0% on the 20 hulls
common to both arms (bars run-case.sh enforces), paired McNemar
8 improved / 1 regressed, p = 0.039. On the stricter zero-wrongly-
oriented proxy it is 35.0% -> 55.0%, p = 0.29, NOT significant.
THE CAP IS NOT MONOTONE PER HULL. Hull 18 went clean -> FAIL (skew 6.19 ->
70.98); hull 12's zero-volume cells went 4 -> 30. A global constant helps on
aggregate and hurts specific hulls, so a per-hull adaptive request is the
next lever, not a further global tweak.
AND THE MECHANISM IN COMMIT 48e190b IS WRONG. It claims clean results sit at
achieved >= 4.3 and failures below 3. Across all four arms there are 20 clean
results below 4.3 and 18 failures at or above 3.0; at cap 7 the failures span
3.99-6.09, fully overlapping the clean range. The cap works. The explanation
attached to it does not, and no replacement mechanism is claimed here.

why_red: GAP D11. THIS WAS A PROSE STRING UNTIL 2026-08-07, AND THAT IS THE
FINDING. Gate 4's suite passes everything it asserts — including
`f < 0.99`, which is the HONEST assertion of a missed bar — so the
ladder printed GREEN while the plan's headline generative clause was
unmet. The 2026-08-06 fix wrote the shortfall into Gate 4's `scope`
text, in a file whose own dataclass documents `detail` as 'human
context; NEVER load-bearing'. A `scope` is no more load-bearing: the
measurement could be softened, reworded or deleted by editing one
string and NOTHING would fail. That is gap D1 — 'RED' -> 'AMBER' bought
exit 0 — surviving in the one place D1's own fix did not reach.
The clause is now Gate 4F, a typed RED row, and this entry is what makes
it fail: an unrecorded red is a NEW break, and past review_by is a
failure too. The bar was NOT softened; 99% is the BuildPlan's number.
MEASURED 2026-08-07, both implementations, same fit and same draw:
GMM  (HullFamilyModel, shipped)   79.33%   <- the watermark
pPCA (PPCAGenerator)              88.67%
The pPCA latent already in the repository BEATS the model shipped as the
generative one. Neither is close to 99%.
AND NOTE WHICH NUMBER THIS IS. Feasibility read off `sample()` is 100%
for ANY proposal distribution whatsoever, because `grammar.check` sits
INSIDE its rejection loop — it measures the loop, not the model, and
Gate 4's bar was reading it. `raw_feasibility()` asks the model. The two
are kept demonstrably different by
tests/test_surrogate_honesty.py::test_feasibility_measured_on_the_sampler
_is_100_percent_by_construction, so the bar cannot be quietly re-pointed
at the tautology.
CLEARING CONDITION: the guided-tabular-diffusion upgrade behind
`HullGenerator` (PLM section 6, owner ml-engineer, READY on PyTorch-MPS)
raising raw feasibility to >= 99%, re-measured with the `verify` command
above. Swapping the shipped implementation to pPCA would be an honest
+9.34 points and still RED — record the new watermark, do not delete

Gate 6D.metric: worst of the two developed hull panels of the TWO-SIDED max distance between the REFOLDED panel and the hull's moulded surface, from unroll.refold_surface_deviation_mm. The edge-only unroll.refold_deviation_mm is recorded beside it and is NO LONGER the watermark: it watches only the panel's far edge, and a pairing with an uncapped ruling step scores 0.07 mm on it while the panel misses the chine by 97.5 mm
Gate 6D.units: mm, reference hull Hull(mid_params(), n_stations=41), rulings="developable" (the default). Per panel, two-sided (edge-only in brackets): bottom-stbd 48.1 (29.2), topside-stbd 66.2 (66.2). The watermark is the worse of the two. THE SAME HULL AND THE SAME METRIC on the pre-2026-08-11 constant-x rulings, which hull_panels(hull, "constant-x") still reproduces verbatim: bottom-stbd 140.2 (141.0), topside-stbd 224.5 (225.7), worst 224.5 -- so 224.5 -> 66.2 is measured under one metric, not manufactured by changing it
Gate 6D.bar: <= 5 mm (REFOLD_BAR_MM in tests/test_manufacturing.py; NavalArchAI BuildPlan section 12.3, 'panels re-fold to the hull within the stated millimetre bar')
Gate 6D.measured_on: tests/test_manufacturing.py fixtures, this working tree, python 3 + numpy. Re-measured at 161 stations on the same hull: 64.1 / 102.2 mm developable against 143.1 / 203.4 constant-x -- BOTH families get WORSE with refinement, so it still does not refine away. Two rejection-sampled grammar hulls at 41 stations, worst panel: 627.6 -> 424.8 mm and 1272.5 -> 885.1 mm, so the improvement is not specific to the reference hull; on one of them the bottom panel's fit was NOT better and hull_panels fell back to constant-x, which panel.rulings records
Gate 6D.verify: python -c "from navalai.geometry import Hull; from navalai.unroll import hull_panels, refold_deviation_mm, refold_surface_deviation_mm; from tests.test_phase0 import mid_params; h=Hull(mid_params(), n_stations=41); print({p.name: (round(refold_surface_deviation_mm(h,p),1), round(float(refold_deviation_mm(p).max()),1)) for p in hull_panels(h)})"  (and: python -m pytest tests/test_manufacturing.py -q -k 'refold or ruling or sheer')
why_red: GAP G4, AND IT IS GAP D11's SHAPE FOUND A SECOND TIME. Until
2026-08-11 this clause had no row that could fail. Gate 6M printed
GREEN because tests/test_manufacturing.py PASSES -- and one of the
things it passes is
test_gate6_refold_clause_is_red_on_the_hull, which asserts
`db.max() > REFOLD_BAR_MM and dt.max() > REFOLD_BAR_MM`. The suite is
green BECAUSE the bar is missed. That test is honest and it stays; what
it is not is a VERDICT. Outside it the only statement of the shortfall
was one sentence in ALIGNMENT.md's STEP/IGES/DXF row -- prose, in a
document, with no owner and no expiry, which is exactly the state gap
D11 recorded for the generative feasibility clause before it became
Gate 4F.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is geometry rather than tolerance. Until
2026-08-11 `hull_panels` took its rulings at CONSTANT STATION x, so the
ruling direction r lay in the y-z plane and det(A', r, r') collapsed to
A'_x (r x r')_x, which vanishes only where the section shape stops
changing. That is why the AFT HALF of the bottom panel -- flat keel,
constant deadrise, i.e. a PLANE -- refolded to 0.008 mm while the
forefoot, where the deadrise warps 8 deg to 30 deg, refolded 141.0 mm off.
THE CLEARING CONDITION WAS ATTEMPTED IN FULL AND IT IS NOT SUFFICIENT.
`unroll.developable_pairing` now solves for SLANTED rulings: the ruling
from keel station i lands at chine parameter v[i] != x[i], v is PINNED at
both ends so the panel still spans the whole edge, and the interior is
solved by Levenberg-Marquardt on the per-quad planarity condition with a
lambda ladder and a multigrid in the station count. It is deterministic
from the identity start and costs 0.63 s for both panels. WHAT IT BOUGHT,
worst panel, reference hull, 41 stations: 224.5 -> 66.2 mm two-sided,
225.7 -> 66.2 mm edge-only. A 3.4x improvement against a bar that is still
missed by 13x.
THREE MECHANISMS HOLD THE REST AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS A RULING CHOICE. (a)
NO EXACT DEVELOPABLE SPANS THE BOTTOM PANEL'S TWO EDGES. Marching the
planar-quad condition forward from the transom TERMINATES at keel x = 7.25
m of 10.00: no plane through the current ruling meets the chine ahead. The
fit can still reach machine-zero warp with both ends pinned -- by putting
1.846 m of chine, 7.4x the mean station spacing, into ONE quad whose chord
then misses the chine by 97.5 mm. (b) THE SHEER POLYLINE IS ALREADY 65.6
mm OFF THE SHEER CURVE at 41 stations, before developability is asked
about, converging at about O(h^0.5): 81.0 / 65.6 / 47.3 / 29.9 mm at 21 /
41 / 81 / 161 stations. `y_sheer = ys * w**0.15` drives dy/dx to infinity
at the stem. That is the floor the 66.2 mm topside sits on and it is a
GRAMMAR property. The chine, whose plan-form carries no such exponent,
reads 3.4 mm at the same 41 stations. (c) THE CHINE AND SHEER HAVE A SLOPE
DISCONTINUITY at x = x_mb * L (5.50 m here), where the plan-form exponent
switches branches and dw/dx jumps 0.1364 -> 0. The fitted topside refolds
to 0.69-0.92 mm aft of that crease and steps to 6.02-6.16 mm at exactly
that station and stays there, so the crease costs a 6 mm floor on its own
-- larger than the whole bar.
THE METRIC WAS MADE STRICTER, NOT LOOSER, IN THE SAME CHANGE. The
watermark used to be the edge-only `refold_deviation_mm`, and case (a)
above is that metric being BOUGHT: the uncapped fit reads 0.07 mm on it
with the panel 97.5 mm off the hull, and a ONE-SIDED panel-to-hull test
scores it perfect too, because every point of that chord lies between keel
and chine and is therefore ON the hull surface.
`refold_surface_deviation_mm` is two-sided and is now the watermark; the
constant-x control is re-measured under it (224.5) so the improvement
cannot be an artefact of the change. tests/test_manufacturing.py::test_the
_edge_only_refold_can_be_bought_and_the_ two_sided_one_cannot fires that
guard by removing the bound, and
::test_the_constant_x_control_is_worse_on_both_panels_and_both_metrics
runs the verbatim old ruling selection through the same measurement.
WHAT DID NOT WORK, recorded so it is not retried. (1) Letting BOTH edges
be reparametrised reached 30.4 mm on the topside but only from a random
start (44.6 mm from the identity), cost 16-18 s per panel against 0.63,
and was not reproducible -- shipped as single-edge. (2) A cubic spline
through the 41 stations, used before `Hull.edge_curves` existed, is itself
94.95 mm off the analytic sheer, so the first fits were measured against
the wrong hull; the closed form is now evaluated directly at the fitted
parameters. (3) An acceptance guard comparing max |quad_warp| instead of
the gate's own metric accepted a fit that was 1938 mm off on a rejection-
sampled hull at 161 stations against 612 mm for the constant-x family it
replaced -- a guard that watches a proxy passes the case the proxy cannot
see. (4) Bounding the ruling step to 2.0x the mean spacing costs the worst
panel 66.2 -> 93.6 mm; uncapping it costs 66.2 -> 97.5. `_MAX_RULING_STEP`
= 4.0 is CALIBRATED over three hulls and two station counts, not derived,
and the code says so.
IT STILL DOES NOT REFINE AWAY, on either ruling family: at 161 stations
the fitted panels read 64.1 / 102.2 mm and the constant-x control 143.1 /
203.4. tests/test_manufacturing.py::test_refold_does_not_converge_with_sta
tion_count pins both.
THE BAR IS NOT SOFTENED. REFOLD_BAR_MM is still 5.0, declared once in
tests/test_manufacturing.py, and both panels and every station are still
measured. This entry's `bar` field points AT that constant rather than
restating it.
NEXT, AND IT IS NOT MORE UNROLLER WORK. (b) and (c) are properties of
`geometry.station_geometry`: the `w**0.15` sheer envelope and the fore/aft
plan-form branch switch at x_mb. Clearing 5 mm needs a sheer taper with
bounded dy/dx at the stem and a C1 join at x_mb, or a hull whose panels
are developable BY CONSTRUCTION -- a change to the hull-geometry kernel
and to what the ladder floats, not to the unroller. That is why owner and
review_by are unchanged.
REVIEW_BY 2026-11-11, UNCHANGED. The work that remains is bigger than the
work that was done, and the date is clear of the 2026-09-06 pair (Gate 2M,
Gate 2U) and of the 6R/6M cluster so the November rows expire on separate
days.
OWNER chief-architect, UNCHANGED, and now more clearly right: what remains
is in the hull-geometry kernel (PLM section 1), which is platform law.

Gate 3E.metric: median relative error of the L1 Wh/NM surrogate on held-out in-support hulls, taken ACROSS query seeds (median of the five per-seed medians)
Gate 3E.units: fraction (0.183 = 18.3%), GP.fit on sample_valid(250, MissionSpec(), seed=7), log(Wh/NM), fit seed 1
Gate 3E.measured_on: five held-out draws of 35 hulls, sample_valid(35, MissionSpec(), seed=s) for s in (991, 992, 993, 994, 995), each filtered by gp.is_ood(Xt, 0.5). Per seed: 991 -> 0.1056 (27/35 kept), 992 -> 0.1830 (33/35), 993 -> 0.2222 (31/35), 994 -> 0.1798 (34/35), 995 -> 0.2340 (33/35). Across-seed median 0.1830, spread 2.22x. 2-sigma coverage holds on every seed (0.818-0.968 against the 0.75 bar), so this row is about the ERROR bar and not the band.
why_red: GAP D10. THE ERROR BAR WAS ONE SAMPLE, AND IT WAS THE BEST OF FIVE.
`test_surrogate_on_l1_physics` drew its held-out set at seed 991 and
asserted `np.median(rel) < 0.15`. MEASURED 2026-08-12 on four further
honest seeds, same training draw and same fit: 0.1830, 0.2222, 0.1798,
0.2340. 991 is the MINIMUM of the five and the only one that clears the
bar. The gate was reading a favourable draw as a property of the model,
which is the same class of defect as a GCI computed on one grid or a
coefficient quoted from one instant of an oscillating force history.
THE BAR WAS NOT MOVED. 0.15 is Gate 3's own number and it stands. What
changed is that the shortfall is now MEASURED across seeds, asserted in
tests/test_phase3.py::test_the_l1_error_bar_is_measured_across_seeds_and_
it_misses_the_bar (which asserts the shortfall EXISTS, so it fails the
day the model improves), and carried here as a typed RED row rather than
hidden behind a green suite. Gate 3 itself stays GREEN for what it does
assert -- co-kriging rho, OOD refusal that separates error, batched-EI
infill -- and the seed lottery around it is this row.
NOT A SEED-SELECTION FIX. Re-pinning to a different seed would move the
number without measuring anything; the five seeds are fixed in
tests/test_phase3.py::L1_QUERY_SEEDS and seed 7 is deliberately excluded
because it is the TRAINING draw (median error exactly 0.0000, a self-test
dressed as a held-out measurement).
CLEARING CONDITION: the across-seed median falling to <= 0.15. The
candidates are more training data (n=250 today), the co-kriging arm once
it has a real high-fidelity tier (gap I1, still open), or a calibration
pass on the GP (gap I5). Record the new watermark on any improvement; do
not delete this entry until the bar is MET, and delete it the moment it
is -- a GREEN gate still listed here is itself a failure.
